Mark measurements inside consecutive repeat windows

Source: R/Mark_ConsecutiveRepeats.R
Mark_ConsecutiveRepeats.Rd

`r lifecycle::badge("experimental")`

Returns every non-missing measurement in the order [Detect_ConsecutiveRepeats()] evaluates it, marked when it sits inside a rolling window of `nWindowLength` identical consecutive values. Both functions share the same ordering and window logic, so summing `window_start` per subject reproduces the `Numerator` of [Detect_ConsecutiveRepeats()].

Usage

Mark_ConsecutiveRepeats(
  df,
  strValueCol,
  strSubjectCol = "subjid",
  strDateCol = "vs_dt",
  strOrderCol = NULL,
  strMeasureCol = NULL,
  strMeasureVal = NULL,
  nWindowLength = 3
)

Arguments

df

`data.frame` One row per measurement record.

strValueCol

`character` Column holding the measurement value.

strSubjectCol

`character` Subject identifier column. Default `"subjid"`.

strDateCol

`character` Date/ordering column. Default `"vs_dt"`.

strOrderCol

`character` Optional column(s) used, in order, to break ties on `strDateCol` (e.g. an intra-visit measurement time or `"visit"`). Default `NULL`, in which case tied records keep their input order.

strMeasureCol

`character` Optional column identifying the measure, for long-format data. When supplied, `df` is filtered to `strMeasureVal`.

strMeasureVal

`character` Value of `strMeasureCol` to keep. Required when `strMeasureCol` is supplied.

nWindowLength

`numeric` Window length; a whole number >= 2. Default `3`.

Value

`df` without rows whose value is missing, ordered by subject, then `strDateCol`, then `strOrderCol`, with three columns added: * `seq`: position of the measurement within its subject. * `in_repeat_window`: `TRUE` when the measurement belongs to at least one all-identical window. * `window_start`: `TRUE` when the window starting at this measurement is all-identical. Its per-subject sum is the repeat-window count.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  subjid = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5),
  vs_dt = rep(as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:4, 2),
  weight = c(10, 10, 5, 3, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10)
)
Mark_ConsecutiveRepeats(df, "weight")
#>    subjid      vs_dt weight seq in_repeat_window window_start
#> 1       A 2024-01-01     10   1            FALSE        FALSE
#> 2       A 2024-01-02     10   2            FALSE        FALSE
#> 3       A 2024-01-03      5   3            FALSE        FALSE
#> 4       A 2024-01-04      3   4            FALSE        FALSE
#> 5       A 2024-01-05     10   5            FALSE        FALSE
#> 6       B 2024-01-01     10   1             TRUE         TRUE
#> 7       B 2024-01-02     10   2             TRUE         TRUE
#> 8       B 2024-01-03     10   3             TRUE         TRUE
#> 9       B 2024-01-04     10   4             TRUE        FALSE
#> 10      B 2024-01-05     10   5             TRUE        FALSE
